evals.prompt: Add a new example to this repo for RabbitMQ with the management UI plugin enabled, similar to how the other single-node services here are set up.
evals.expected_output: A new rabbitmq/ directory with docker-compose.yml (private_net network, named volume for data, container_name/hostname set, version 3.3, source comment) and README.md (Purpose/Features/Docker Management/IDE Integration sections, management UI URL and default login called out), plus a new row added to the root README.md table.
assertions: New service directory exists containing a docker-compose.yml
docker-compose.yml pins version '3.3' matching the rest of the repo
docker-compose.yml sets container_name and hostname explicitly for the rabbitmq service
docker-compose.yml joins a bridge network named private_net (reuses repo convention, doesn't invent a new network name)
docker-compose.yml has a named volume with a comment noting docker-compose prefixes the actual volume name with the directory name
Management UI port (15672) is exposed in docker-compose.yml
README.md contains the four standard section headers: # Purpose, # Features, # Docker Management, # IDE Integration
README.md's # Docker Management section links back to the root README with the repo's stock wording
Root README.md table has a new row for the RabbitMQ example

evals.expected_output: elasticsearch/.env.template (and .env if present) MEM_LIMIT and/or heap-related values adjusted to fit a 2GB budget across the 3-node cluster, using the existing MEM_LIMIT env-var pattern rather than hardcoding values into docker-compose.yml. README.md updated if the documented behavior/values change. Root README Min Memory column updated if it names a concrete number.
assertions: Memory change is expressed through the existing MEM_LIMIT env-var pattern in .env/.env.template rather than hardcoded directly into docker-compose.yml
Per-node mem_limit values across the 3 ES nodes (plus Kibana if included) sum to roughly a 2GB total budget, not left at the old default
docker-compose.yml's service structure (node count, healthchecks, networks, volumes) is otherwise left intact -- no gratuitous unrelated rewrite
README.md or .env.template comments reflect the new memory guidance if the old value was documented anywhere
Root README.md Min Memory column for elasticsearch is updated if it previously stated a concrete number

evals.prompt: The kafka-confluent example in this repo is pinned to Confluent Platform 5.5.1, which is really old at this point. Can you upgrade it to whatever the current recommended Confluent all-in-one docker-compose baseline is, not just bump the version number?
evals.expected_output: kafka-confluent/docker-compose.yml image tags moved consistently to a current Confluent Platform version across all services, following today's upstream cp-all-in-one baseline (re-derived from the upstream links in the file's header comments) rather than a mechanical find/replace of '5.5.1'. If the current upstream baseline structurally differs from the old one (e.g. Zookeeper vs KRaft), the agent should surface that as a decision rather than silently picking one. README.md References/Features updated to match, and the old version noted somewhere as having been replaced.
assertions: No image tag in kafka-confluent/docker-compose.yml still reads 5.5.1

All confluentinc platform image tags (cp-server, cp-zookeeper or its replacement, cp-schema-registry, cp-enterprise-control-center, ksqldb images, cp-kafka-rest) are bumped to the same new platform version consistently, not a partial upgrade
SUMMARY.md or README.md explicitly calls out what upstream changed structurally between the old and new baseline (e.g. Zookeeper vs KRaft), rather than being silent about it
README.md's # References links are checked/updated against the current upstream doc/repo locations
Old version (5.5.1) is noted somewhere as the version being replaced (SUMMARY.md, README, or commit-style note), so the upgrade is traceable
